I've tested locally on a Pixel 8 Pro and unfortunately on that device this causes a slight performance regression in the TPS demo. With a Directional light with shadows added I get 40 FPS on master and 36 FPS with this PR. I'm trying to figure out where the extra time goes, but the monitor shows it all coming from shadow rendering. 

So far I have confirmed that the draw list is opened the correct number of times and the correct number of passes are rendered. The output looks correct as well. ~My current theory is that the passes aren't getting handled by the acyclic graph as nicely as before because of using the viewport instead of the draw lists.~ It looks like the same graph level us used regardless of adding this or now. I'm really not sure what is accounting for the difference in performance

Ugh. I'll check out what's going on.

40 -> 36 FPS is not a minor regression. That's a huge 2.77ms difference.

It's probably some overlapping thing. Even though Mobile doesn't have async compute, they still try to overlap VS and PS workloads.

I assume this was TPS in Mobile renderer right? (I know it's a stupid question, but I've gotta ask).

> I assume this was TPS in Mobile renderer right? (I know it's a stupid question, but I've gotta ask).

Yep, TPS demo, mobile renderer. Using the version from the Forge PR, but with a Directional Light (with shadows) added. 

I confirmed in renderdoc that the PR is working as expected (using one long render pass with dynamic viewport and scissor instead of multiple render passes. It just takes an extra 2 ms for rendering shadows (which is confirmed by printing the GPU profile while running)

# Updates

We talked with ARM. Since I don't know how much is covered by NDA, I'll just stick to major points that were known beforehand:

1. My guesses were right. The problem is that more Render Passes result in better scheduling overlap of VS and PS work between those passes. The benefit of using better Clear semantics instead of Clear-then-Load is not as big as expected due to certain clever HW optimizations that reduce the expected bandwidth gap between our old and new path.
2. Since there seems to be no difference in Adreno either, this optimization done by TheForge don't seem to have an application in Android and should not be merged.
3. There _might_ still be an application on iOS and M1/M2/etc GPUs. However I couldn't test it since the newest iPhone I have is the iPhone 8, which could not run the demo, seemingly due to HW feature limitations.
4. I went back to the drawing board + some suggestions for ARM, found there was still _something_ we could do, which I will elaborate.


## New optimization

We know that in Vulkan the following is the ideal path for a TBDR (Desktop is another story):

1. Each directional light pass uses Clear semantics instead of Load semantics.
2. Each directional light pass lives in its own Render Pass.

Based on this, I **pushed a new commit** to make the following changes:

1. Added `SUPPORTS_NATIVE_RENDER_AREA_CLEAR` feature flag. When present, it means the optimization is much more likely to be an optimization (and not just a performance net negative). When absent, the old code is used.
   - This is because Metal only allows to clear the whole texture and not just the render area / subregion. Which means MoltenVK (and our Metal backend) must turn to emulation when the clear is only applied to the sub region.
   - Desktop GPUs are more troublesome because some of them (e.g. Vega/RDNA + NVIDIA post Turing or Ampere?) do benefit slightly from Clear semantics, but on the other hand they benefit a lot from the full-region clear operation being done in parallel with async compute. Which is why Forward+ backend still uses the old code.
3. When present, each directional light pass clears its render area.
4. Additionally, removed unused variables (from both Mobile and Forward+ backend).

I know that PRs are encouraged to submit a single commit per PR. I will squash the commits once I get confirmation these changes are ok.

**How to test:** Set `render_pass_opts_enabled` to false and compare before this PR. Performance should be equal or higher, but not lower.


**Update:** Since it's easy to get lost in what changed in [my commit](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100321/commits/966c083d189493c8f66bf8b55506a590969fa3c1) due to functions having dozens of arguments, it all boils down to the following (pseudo code):

**Before:**
```cpp
clear( directional_light_atlas );

for( directional_lights )
    _render_shadow_pass( clear_region = false );
```

**After:**
```cpp

const bool clear_directional_lights_by_region =
			RD::get_singleton()->has_feature(RD::SUPPORTS_NATIVE_RENDER_AREA_CLEAR);

if( !clear_directional_lights_by_region )
    clear( directional_light_atlas );

for( directional_lights )
    _render_shadow_pass( clear_region = clear_directional_lights_by_region );
```

That's it.
Is there anything I could test / analyse for Apple GPUs?

> Is there anything I could test / analyse for Apple GPUs?

Yes!

1. Download [this demo](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1wg1PLTlc6pZs-HzFzQEGAkN3Oo7sqAfB/view?usp=sharing).
    - Remember "fix" (enable) ETC2/ASTC and that it requires you to restart the editor, or else it will crash when trying to run on device
3. Compile this PR for iOS (macOS for ARM should work too I suppose). Test running the demo in the following scenarios:
    1. After PR, with `render_pass_opts_enabled = true`.
    2. After PR, with `render_pass_opts_enabled = false`.
    4. Before PR

If we add the native Metal backend (besides MoltenVK), that'd be 6 tests.

Compare the framerate (the demo already has an FPS counter).

I've tested with three devices Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 7, and Pixel 4. 

I tested all devices with `render_pass_opts_enabled = true` and without this PR. I only tested the Pixel 8 Pro with  `render_pass_opts_enabled = false`, 

**Pixel 8 Pro**
No significant change in any case. 

**Pixel 7**
0.4 mspf improvement with `render_pass_opts_enabled = true`

**Pixel 4**
0.2-0.3 mspf improvement with `render_pass_opts_enabled = true`. To test this I had to set the 3d scale down to 0.4 and turn off all lights except for the directional light.
Heads up that I am on a plane from Phoenix, Arizona to Australia, so I'll be mostly offline for the next 30 hours, in case that is important.

>

Wait, what?

To be clear: I did **NOT** touch the case of `render_pass_opts_enabled = true`.
So if previously it was giving lower perf, it shouldn't be giving better perf now!

The case I was most interested was `render_pass_opts_enabled = false` after vs before PR.

> **Pixel 8 Pro** No significant change in any case.

WHAAAA?

You already tested this phone and toggling `render_pass_opts_enabled` was previously giving you 40 FPS -> 36 FPS.

Did you set the atlas to 4096 instead of the default 2048? (to stress test the shadows) like you did last time?

> **Pixel 7** 0.4 mspf improvement with `render_pass_opts_enabled = true`

Pixel 7 is Mali-G710 MP7 (Valhall). This goes against your findings in Pixel 8 Pro and my findings in Samsung A54 (Mali-G68 MP5, also Valhall).

:confused: 

> **Pixel 4** 0.2-0.3 mspf improvement with `render_pass_opts_enabled = true`. To test this I had to set the 3d scale down to 0.4 and turn off all lights except for the directional light.

Interesting test. I also have an Adreno 640 for testing. I did not see a difference (all tests 6 FPS) but I suspected I was bottlenecked by something else.

I could try the same trick you're doing to see if I see an improvement.

> Heads up that I am on a plane from Phoenix, Arizona to Australia, so I'll be mostly offline for the next 30 hours, in case that is important.

No rush. This PR has been in the pipeline for a month or more.

It turns out I built release templates, but run debug templates. Thanks to our Android buildsystem caching, I managed to run the same benchmark three times. The reason I got a performance differential was likely due to thermal throttling, as I run the scene multiple times and recorded the average frame time from the worst run. Plus I always tested this PR after testing master. 

I ran the benchmark again for each device and got the following consistent results. This time I let the devices cool down and ran the benchmark in different orders.

It seems on Mali devices there is a consistent loss in performance with this PR. While with Adreno there is a slight improvement, but only when `render_pass_opts_enabled = true`.

Pixel 8 Pro
Master: 23.6 mspf
render_pass_opts_enabled = false: 24.2 mspf
render_pass_opts_enabled = true: 25.6 mspf

Pixel 7
Reporting shadow time only since there is too much fluctuation in full frame time
Master: 7.20 mspf
render_pass_opts_enabled = false: 7.78 mspf
render_pass_opts_enabled = true: 9.15 mspf

Pixel 4
Reporting shadow time only since there is too much fluctuation in full frame time
Master: 11.56 mspf
render_pass_opts_enabled = false: 18.70 mspf
render_pass_opts_enabled = true: 11.35 mspf

OK, hard data is hard:

| Adreno 640   | Original TPS                        | master branch                                     | 179,06 | 5,58  | 180,83        | 5,53         |
| Adreno 640   | Only directional light + 0,25 scale | render_pass_opts_enabled = true                   | 46,08  | 21,70 | 62,10         | 16,10        |
| Adreno 640   | Only directional light + 0,25 scale | render_pass_opts_enabled = false; clear subregion | 48,52  | 20,61 | 65,10         | 15,36        |
| Adreno 640   | Only directional light + 0,25 scale | master branch                                     | 46,07  | 21,71 | 62,32         | 16,05        |
| Mali-G68 MP5 | Original TPS                        | render_pass_opts_enabled = true                   | 78,62  | 12,72 | 80,04         | 12,49        |
| Mali-G68 MP5 | Original TPS                        | render_pass_opts_enabled = false; clear subregion | 73,19  | 13,66 | 75,02         | 13,33        |
| Mali-G68 MP5 | Original TPS                        | master branch                                     | 73,90  | 13,53 | 76,28         | 13,11        |
| Mali-G68 MP5 | Only directional light + 0,5 scale  | render_pass_opts_enabled = true                   | 42,88  | 23,32 | 49,95         | 20,02        |
| Mali-G68 MP5 | Only directional light + 0,5 scale  | render_pass_opts_enabled = false; clear subregion | 37,95  | 26,35 | 42,20         | 23,70        |
| Mali-G68 MP5 | Only directional light + 0,5 scale  | master branch                                     | 37,48  | 26,68 | 42,36         | 23,61        |

This data was gathered using debugger's profiler:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb0e81a7-f3f1-4ede-a796-8643643e0c1a)

It conveniently supports exporting to CSV (where I can calculate avg and 99th percentiles). It also provides the most accurate counter for these measurements: "Frame Time".

Well... the data is disheartening: On Adreno 640, TheForge's optimization is indistinguishable from noise. While my optimization causes a slowdown.
On Mali-G68, TheForge's optimization causes a very visible slowdown. While my optimization is this time the one indistinguishable from noise.

We could try to contact ARM for further help, but at this point I'm more inclined to just close the pull request and abort the merge.

> We could try to contact ARM for further help, but at this point I'm more inclined to just close the pull request and abort the merge.

Unfortunately I have to agree. I think we have pushed this PR as far as it can go. It seems like the current code is not always the most efficient, but it is never the least efficient. Anything we change makes the code more complex and risks hitting a performance cliff on one driver or another. 

I'll go ahead and close this and mark it as salvageable in case we ever have a reason to come back to this optimization.
